objective: Deliver the frozen provider design as a repository-local reference workflow with seven component-sized implementation packets. Each packet names the affected operator path, observable completion outcome, sufficient context, pragmatic black-box proof when practical, and a concrete impracticality reason plus substitute when black-box proof is not practical. The existing Rust workspace and provider crate fix repository file ownership; this plan resolves cross-task handoff interfaces, while implementation remains free to choose replaceable internal mechanisms inside frozen decisions and those handoffs.

tasks.objective: Define strict request and result contracts, dispatch behavior, static topology description, and caller-selected profile freeze semantics without conflating inspectable run input with describe.
deliverables: Provider crate manifest in fictional-repo/provider/Cargo.toml

Exact provider protocol contract implementation in fictional-repo/provider/src/protocol.rs and fictional-repo/provider/src/main.rs: flat describe request {"operation":"describe"}; flat evaluate request fields operation, workflow, initial_input, context, transition, prior_evaluations; reject unknown fields; describe returns one workflow object with exactly the top-level fields id, initial_state, states, transitions, and work_slots; each state has exactly id, title, instructions, and final; each transition has exactly source, event, target, and kind; each work slot has exactly id, state, and event; evaluate returns exactly {"result":"allow"}, {"result":"unsupported"}, or {"result":"deny","feedback":{"code","message","details"?}}; exit 0 means valid response written, 1 evaluation/config failure with stderr/no stdout response, 2 protocol/usage failure with stderr/no stdout response; one request/process.

Repository context contract: the existing Rust workspace fixes file ownership only; src/protocol.rs and src/main.rs are task boundaries, not new design-level architecture, and replaceable private helpers remain unconstrained.

Frozen profile-selection and inspection contract: caller selects one full canonical profile and passes that exact value as start initial_input; Loop Engine freezes exact initial_input; show projects frozen initial_input unchanged; flat evaluate carries the same frozen initial_input; describe does not expose selected profile policies or artifact schemas

Protocol contract tests in fictional-repo/provider/tests/describe_protocol.rs preserve and compare against the existing committed pre-change snapshot at fictional-repo/provider/tests/snapshots/describe.json; the worker must not author a replacement topology from the new implementation
out_of_scope: Schema validation, evidence aggregation, checked-transition routing, and semantic review judgment
Workflow state mutation and documentation integration
validation: Assert malformed JSON and unknown operations return protocol errors without stdout, unknown evaluate envelope fields are rejected, and flat describe output matches fictional-repo/provider/tests/snapshots/describe.json byte-for-byte as only the exact static workflow topology snapshot; selected profile policies and artifact schemas are not in describe; caller-selected full canonical profile survives start initial_input freeze, show projects frozen initial_input unchanged, and flat evaluate carries that exact frozen initial_input. The separate public scenario also asserts a user-visible outcome rather than only process exit status.

Drive the affected operator path through a practical black-box scenario and assert the observable result. Where an unavailable platform makes a second black-box path impractical, state that concrete reason and use the nearest scripted provider-boundary substitute; do not treat command exit activity alone as proof.
